knowledge:
- key_parameters: hierarchy_method=Determines the hierarchical aggregation method to construct the tree; defaults to "hopach", but can be any method in hclust (e.g., "ward.D", "ward.D2", "single", "complete", "average", "mcquitty", "median", "centroid") ;; sig_test=The significance test to use, either default (t-test/Wilcoxon) or count models ("GLMM" or "edgeR") ;; pos_class_name=The name of the positive class of interest for significance testing (e.g., "COV" or NULL) ;; phylo=A phylogenetic tree object (e.g., clust_tree$clust_tree) representing the cluster hierarchy
- alternatives: hopach vs hclust methods (like "average") for tree construction; edgeR or GLMM count models vs default t-test/Wilcoxon for significance testing
- when_to_use: When analyzing single-cell cytometry or single-cell expression data to identify which cell subpopulation proportions (relative to total cells or parent nodes) are significantly associated with patient clinical outcomes
- pitfalls: Ensure the input expression matrix is transposed correctly (cells as rows, markers as columns) ;; Ensure cluster, class, and sample vectors are of length equal to the number of cells ;; Interactive plotting may remove rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range

workflows.name: hierarchical_cell_subpopulation_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify robust associations between hierarchical cell subsets and clinical outcomes from single-cell cytometry data.
input: exprs (matrix of single-cell marker expressions, cells as rows, markers as columns)
classes (vector of patient clinical outcomes/classes per cell)
samples (vector of patient/sample IDs per cell)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct the hierarchical tree of clusters using getClusterTree ;; 2. Perform significance testing of cell subpopulations using testTree ;; 3. Extract significance results using getTreeResults ;; 4. Visualize results interactively using plotInteractiveHeatmap ;; 5. Extract cell proportions (%total and %parent) using getCellProp ;; 6. Extract marker geometric means per cell type using getCellGMeans
workflows.code:
clust_tree <- getClusterTree(exprs,
                             clusters,
                             hierarchy_method="hopach")

tested_tree <- testTree(phylo=clust_tree$clust_tree,
                      clusters=clusters,
                      samples=samples,
                      classes=classes,
                      pos_class_name=NULL)

res_df <- getTreeResults(tested_tree)

plotInteractiveHeatmap(tested_tree,
                       clust_med_df = clust_tree$median_freq,
                       clusters=clusters)

clust_tree <- getClusterTree(exprs,
                             clusters,
                             hierarchy_method="average")

tested_tree <- testTree(clust_tree$clust_tree,
                      clusters=clusters,
                      samples=samples,
                      classes=classes,
                      pos_class_name=NULL)

plotInteractiveHeatmap(tested_tree,
                       clust_med_df = clust_tree$median_freq,
                       clusters=clusters)

clust_tree <- getClusterTree(exprs,
                             clusters,
                             hierarchy_method="hopach")

tested_tree_edgeR <- testTree(clust_tree$clust_tree,
                      clusters=clusters,
                      samples=samples,
                      classes=classes,
                      sig_test="edgeR",
                      pos_class_name="COV")

plotInteractiveHeatmap(tested_tree_edgeR,
                       clust_med_df = clust_tree$median_freq,
                       clusters=clusters)

head(tested_tree_edgeR$data[,c("parent", "node", "isTip", "clusters", "FDR_parent", "FDR_total")])

prop_df <- getCellProp(phylo=clust_tree$clust_tree,
                       clusters=clusters,
                       samples=samples,
                       classes=classes)

means_df <- getCellGMeans(clust_tree$clust_tree,
                          exprs=exprs,
                          clusters=clusters,
                          samples=samples,
                          classes=classes)
